en: During Mayon Volcano eruptions, falling ash can trigger asthma, so residents must wear N95 masks to protect their lungs.
Because the Philippines faces roughly 20 typhoons yearly, coastal families in Cagayan must prepare emergency go-bags before the rainy season.
The active West Valley Fault runs through Metro Manila, so residents must secure heavy furniture to prevent earthquake injuries.
Tuguegarao City frequently records the highest heat index in the Philippines, making constant hydration crucial to prevent heatstroke.
Stagnant water in the Agusan Marsh breeds mosquitoes carrying dengue fever, so covering water containers is a vital health practice.
Climbing Mount Pulag requires thick jackets because its high altitude drops temperatures below freezing, which can cause fatal hypothermia.
Stepping on venomous sea urchins in the Tubbataha Reefs causes severe pain, making water shoes necessary for safe snorkeling.
Heavy monsoon rains in Benguet province trigger deadly landslides on mountain highways, so drivers must avoid steep slopes during storms.
Wading through floodwaters connected to Laguna de Bay can transmit leptospirosis bacteria, so washing thoroughly with soap afterward is essential.
The clear skies over El Nido, Palawan allow intense ultraviolet radiation to reach the skin, making sunscreen essential to prevent sunburns.
The basin shape of Metro Manila traps vehicle exhaust during dry months, worsening air quality and triggering childhood asthma attacks.
Flash floods in the Cagayan River basin rise rapidly during heavy rains, requiring immediate evacuation to higher ground to survive.
